newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, swap rates fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, swap rates fall sharply.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE ended firmer on Thursday, in line with the steep fall in interest rate swap (IRS) rates, traders said.
The three-year swap rate was quoted at 1.18/1.22 percent, down from Wednesday's 1.24/28 percent.
Some city banks and a long-term credit bank actively received three, five, seven year fixed interest rates, steepening the rate falls across the yield curve, traders said.

The June rose to a high of 99.35 in early trade on renewed speculation that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would not tighten credit until well into the next year after the BOJ's quarterly "tankan" survey showed only slight improvement in corporate sentiment.

"Chances are that the central bank will be able to remove the current cap on short-term rates and let them firm a little in the summer of 1997," said Shoji Kitta, managing director of Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, the largest money broker in Japan.
The one-, two- and three- month certificates of deposits (CDs) were all issued at 0.50 percent.
The BOJ capped the key overnight call rate in September 1995 at 0.5 percent, the level of the official discount rate (ODR), and has kept it there ever since.
Banks which made fixed interest rates payments in the IRS market also bought the June and September Euroyen contacts to hedge against their positions, traders said.

After the day session close, the Trade Ministry said that Japan's industrial production rose a preliminary 3.5 percent in October from September on a seasonally adjusted basis. It also forecast manufacturers' output will be down 1.7 percent in November and down 0.2 percent in December.
In the night session, the June was unchanged at 0711 GMT from the day session settlement.
The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.48 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The BOJ conducted a neutral operation this morning by injecting 100 billion yen into the money market where there was a projected net fund shortfall of 110 billion yen.
